# Secondary position and alignment reference

`secondary_position_reference.json` is generated by
`../scripts/generate_secondary_position_reference.py`. The generator executes
fixed original Matplotlib source through the accepted complete Secondary/numeric
loader. It is self-contained with tracked dependencies; ignored preparation
scripts and JSON are not runtime dependencies, and no port function supplies an
expected result.

Four source profiles are kept distinct:

| Profile | Original records | Typed projection |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Constructor/location/alignment | 43 | 36 scenarios; 7 dynamic-origin/type records remain source-only |
| Actual deferred locator/display geometry | 10 | Two sequential x/y scenarios |
| Complete Base.draw numeric phase | 2 traces | Two x/y scenarios |
| Locator captured before forward callback | 1 trace | One scenario |

These are 56 profile records, projected to 41 private Scene scenario functions in
two registered groups of at most32 scenarios. They are not56 full renderer parity
tests. They are separate from D40's53 and D41's46 observations. Each generated
scenario is isolated with config restoration, and group failures retain the
source ID/label.

The generated files are:

- `secondary_position_reference.json`: full source values, exceptions, state,
  identity facts and traces, with explicit profile boundaries and source hashes.
- `../scene/secondary_position_reference_wbtest.mbt`: typed projections.

## Public state and typed boundary

`SecondaryAxisLocation::Position(Double)` carries a parent-normalized numeric
location alongside the existing four named edges. `SecondaryAxisAlignment` is a
separate four-edge enum. Constructors keep a stable coordinate direction from
`secondary_xaxis` or `secondary_yaxis`; orientation is not inferred from the raw
location after a setter.

`location()` retains the named/numeric tag, `position()` returns its numerical
position, and `alignment()` returns the current decoration side.
`set_location` accepts a compatible named edge or any Double without clipping or
an eager finite guard. `set_alignment` accepts only a side compatible with the
fixed orientation. Wrong named directions fail before mutation. Existing typed
constructor error strings remain their prior checked mapping.

Constructor alignment is selected only once: position<.5 chooses bottom/left;
otherwise it chooses top/right. Exact .5 and NaN choose top/right. Values below0
or above1 are accepted, as are ±Inf and NaN. Later set_location changes the raw
requested position while retaining the existing alignment, own view, four ticker
objects/default flags, scale/cache and active rectangle. Explicit set_alignment
changes the decoration side while retaining the location and active rectangle.

Python Boolean and NumPy Boolean origins, None location and numerical alignment
are retained in the seven source-only records. Python False/True are Real and
accepted; NumPy bool is rejected by the original method. General Python numeric
classes, arbitrary dynamic objects and a supplied location Transform are outside
this Double/named bridge. The source methods' general dynamic protocol is not
silently described as fully migrated.

## Original host and geometry

The complete original Secondary class, `_TransformedBoundsLocator`, actual
Bbox/Transforms, Axis limit/scale/autoscale and numeric aspect bodies execute.
Graphical superclass construction remains the accepted numerical storage/style
host. Spine visibility and tick/label side are explicit presentation stores:
the original method selects their values and write order, but no full graphical
Tick/Text/spine artist state is claimed. Native locator/transform object identity
is recorded without inventing a new public locator-object API in the port.

An axes locator produces the thin normalized box using1e-10 in the cross direction,
then applies the real parent and Figure transforms. Receipt of a new location
replaces that locator but does not eagerly move the child's active rectangle.
The original constructor's active rectangle remains until an aspect stage.
Public direct apply_aspect maps/stores limits and restores the original rectangle;
the positioned hook captures the candidate first, then maps/stores limits, then
commits the candidate active rectangle only after a successful limit store.

The generated whitebox tests pass the original measured parent screen frame to
the positioned hook as a declared context. For the43-record profile, normalized
parent[.2,.2,.4,.6] produces original parent width128.00000000000003. The Scene
convenience rectangle arithmetic can instead produce128; this reference does not
claim complete parent-layout transform parity by substituting that convenience
result. Source frame/context values are recorded independently in JSON. The10
geometry records and later traces use parent[.2,.25,.5,.5], whose actual screen
frame is[64,60,160,120] on a320x240 Figure.

All finite expected values are encoded from original binary64 bits and compared
exactly. Geometry is not simplified to an algebraic line, a constant tolerance,
a different inverse affine or a formula copied from the port. NaN classification
is tested without a NaN payload claim. Complete SVG export for nonfinite placement
is not required by the source presentation host: native NaN receipt and later
all-NaN Bbox storage succeed, and are retained as such rather than a fake setter
validation error.

## Draw phases and callback capture

The two complete draw traces execute original Secondary.draw followed by original
`_AxesBase.draw` with empty graphical artist, compositor, title and renderer-group
sinks. Original locator evaluation and both Secondary.apply_aspect/_set_lims
calls execute. These traces do not claim GUI/glyph or nonempty artist rendering.

A constant forward4/inverse1 and old Fixed major are used across parent linear→log.
The first old-context limits stage produces[3.8,4.2], followed by scale reset.
Base.draw then evaluates the locator and invokes another aspect/limits stage with
the new Log defaults, producing final[1,10]. The generated test asserts both stages.
D40's `[3.8,4.2]` expectation remains correct for its deliberately earlier
super.draw-presentation-sink profile; its generator/JSON are unchanged here.
The public prepare_draw remains that earlier stage. Full owned rendering adds the
positioned aspect stage afterward.

The capture trace uses a forward callback that changes the requested location
from.25 to.75. Original Base.draw-style locator evaluation obtains the candidate
before calling that forward. The final requested position is.75, while the active
rectangle for this call remains the captured.25 rectangle[64,90,160,1.2000000992884452e-8].
The typed projection checks that exact difference. Scalar callback transport does
not claim native vector callback counts or arbitrary Python exception effects.
